name: Linphone
tagline: Open source SIP softphone for voice, video and messaging across desktop and mobile.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The client is free and open source, money sits in Belledonne's commercial licensing, Flexisip server and support contracts.

verdictSummary: A browser softphone is genuinely one-sittable because the browser already ships the hard parts: WebRTC gives you the media stack, echo cancellation, jitter buffer and codecs, and SIP.js gives you registration and call control over WebSocket. What you cannot one-shot is everything Linphone does beyond a dialpad: a native mobile app that wakes on push for an incoming call, ZRTP key verification, SIP over UDP/TCP to providers that have never heard of WebSocket, and the pile of NAT and ICE edge cases that make calls connect on hotel wifi. Also worth saying out loud: Linphone is already free and open source, so the thing you are 'replacing' is a codebase you could just read. The honest reason to build your own is that you want a three-button dialer instead of a full communications client. The honest reason not to is that a phone that misses calls is not a phone.
coreLoopDIY: Registers to your existing SIP account over WebSocket and lets you place, receive and hang up voice calls from a browser tab with a call log.
requirements: A SIP account from a provider or a SIP server you control
That provider must support SIP over secure WebSocket, many do not
HTTPS origin, browsers refuse microphone access otherwise
A STUN server, and a TURN server if you want calls to work behind symmetric NAT
A tab that stays open, because that is your ringer
whatYouLose: Mobile apps that ring when the screen is off, which means push notifications, a push gateway and app store builds
Video calls, screen sharing and group calls unless you build them separately
ZRTP and SRTP media verification, the privacy feature people actually chose Linphone for
Messaging, presence and file transfer over SIP SIMPLE
Support for providers that only speak SIP over UDP or TCP, which is most of them
Codec negotiation beyond whatever your browser happens to offer
moatNotes: The moat is not business model, it is the long tail of broken SIP implementations in the wild that this project has been patching around since the early 2000s.
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays for the Linphone client, they pay Belledonne for commercial licensing to ship it inside a product without GPL obligations, for Flexisip as a hosted or supported server, and for someone to answer the phone when calls stop connecting. That last one is the real product. A DIY browser dialer covers your own desk; it does not cover a fleet of handsets, a push infrastructure, or an auditor asking which media encryption you use.
notes: The dialpad is an afternoon; the part where your phone rings in your pocket at 3am is not.
prompt:
Build a minimal browser softphone as a local, self-hosted web app. No accounts, no backend database, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Vite + TypeScript, vanilla DOM, no framework.
- sip.js for SIP signalling over secure WebSocket.
- Plain CSS, dark, one column, no UI library.
- A tiny Node http server for local HTTPS using a self signed cert via mkcert instructions in the README.

Config comes from .env, loaded with Vite's import.meta.env, and .env is gitignored. Ship a .env.example with:
VITE_SIP_WS_URI, VITE_SIP_URI, VITE_SIP_PASSWORD, VITE_STUN_URI, VITE_TURN_URI, VITE_TURN_USER, VITE_TURN_PASSWORD.

In scope:
- Register to the SIP account on load, show a clear registration state badge: registering, registered, failed, with the failure reason printed verbatim.
- A dialpad plus a text field that accepts a full SIP URI or a bare number that gets appended to the configured domain.
- Place an outbound audio call, show ringing, connected and a live call timer.
- Accept or decline inbound calls with an audible ringtone generated by the Web Audio API, no asset files.
- Mute, hold and hang up buttons. DTMF tones during a call via SIP INFO and RTP, whichever sip.js exposes cleanly.
- Call log of the last 50 calls in localStorage: direction, peer, start time, duration, outcome. Clear button.
- A collapsible log panel that dumps SIP messages and ICE candidate state, because every bug you hit will be in there.

Out of scope, do not build: video, conferencing, messaging, presence, contacts sync, push notifications, mobile apps, SIP over UDP or TCP.

README must state plainly that this only works with providers offering SIP over WebSocket, that microphone access requires HTTPS, and that the tab must stay open to receive calls.
